name: Gulay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: A.T.P.L.G. 2012 phonology (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, not online). Keegan et al. 2014 Lexique Gulay PDF read (morkegbooks.com): tone-marked entries but no stress/prosody statement.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. n.d. Extended Bibliography (Sara-Bagirmi Language Project), 7 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliography only; lists no Gulay-specific work at all (no hit for Gulay/Goulaye/Gulei); Sara-group phonology items are for Mbay, Sar, Ngambay, Gor, Bediondo, Nar, Laka.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Gulay language'; Glottolog 5.x languoid page gula1268
sources.note: Wikipedia gives only an alphabet table (dialects Gulay and Pen); Glottolog page cites only Djarangar 2000 and Ethnologue. Neither says anything about stress.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Central Sara Languages, 9th ed. (The Sara Language Project). Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 505 pp. [Glottolog ref 309963 lists the 2012 2nd ed.]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. General 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' pp. 6-15: three level tones H/M/L on vowels and final sonorants, complex tones on VV and V+sonorant, syllable types CV/CVC (p. 10, 12). 'Introduction to the Gulay Lexicon' pp. 197-199 ('Comments on the Phonology', 'Vowel Patterns', 'Sound Changes') covers consonants, vowel harmony and tone loss before vowel/nasal suffixes; no word 'stress'/'accent' anywhere except in glosses.

sources.citation: Ngaradoumbaye Clément, Nadjirissengar Moise & John M. Keegan. 2014. Lexique Gulay, 5e éd. Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 135 pp. (Glottolog ref 308546)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Two-page French introduction (location, speaker numbers, classification, acknowledgement of Jim Roberts for 'problèmes phonologiques'), then abbreviations and the tone-marked lexicon; no phonology section, nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2000. Identité tonale et filiation des langues sara-bongo-baguirmiennes (Afrique centrale). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Ordered-Received); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number Ordered-Received
sources.note: Comparative tonal study of the SBB group; would establish the tonal (not stress) prosody of Gulay from a second primary author if Gulay data are included.

sources.citation: Huguet, Jean-Pierre. 1986. Phonétique et phonologie: études comparatives au sein du groupe Sara (République du Tchad). Doctoral thesis, Université Paris 3 (Sorbonne Nouvelle), 572 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological description that explicitly covers 'Gulay Occidental' (per Glottolog); a 572-page comparative phonology of 13 Sara varieties is the likeliest place for any remark on accent in Gulay. theses.fr record 1986PA030143 shows no PDF.

sources.citation: Caprile, Jean-Pierre & Jacques Fédry. 1970. Le groupe des langues 'Sara' (République du Tchad). Afrique et Langage, Études linguistiques 4. Lyon.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Survey of the Sara group by the Collège Charles Lwanga linguists whose transcription (tone marking) Keegan adopted; may contain phonological notes per variety including Goulaye. Listed in Keegan's bibliography; not found online.

sources.citation: Tucker, Archibald N. & Margaret A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: Oxford University Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Survey with a section on the Sara group (tone, syllable structure) that sometimes comments on stress; would be second-hand for Gulay. Not full-view online.

sources.citation: Chabrelie, Louis. 1935. Notes sur la langue des Sara, avec un vocabulaire comparatif des différents dialectes. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 5(2): 125-151.

sources.note: Open on Persée but the PDF is behind an altcha challenge; a comparative Sara vocabulary that may include Goulaye and an early remark on accent. Low value (1935 amateur notes).
